newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada gas firms name Pan-Alberta in lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Canada gas firms name Pan-Alberta in lawsuit.

text.p: A heavyweight group of Canadian natural gas producers has named aggregator Pan-Alberta Gas Ltd in a lawsuit that claims the company breached several obligations and robbed them of the potential value of their natural gas, Houston-based NGC Corp, an indirect owner of Pan-Alberta, said on Tuesday.
NGC said the suit asks for damages of C$5 million and other costs. The action also states that actual damages may exceed C$50 million, it said.

"The suit alleges that, since 1992, Pan-Alberta has breached contractual, regulatory and fiduciary obligations that resulted in the plaintiffs' being deprived of the value of the best available netback prices for their natural gas," NGC said in a statement.
The company said it was reviewing the lawsuit and its "preliminary view is that the claims are without merit, and we expect Pan Alberta to vigorously defend its position."

Companies that filed the court action include Anderson Exploration Ltd, Apache Corp unit Apache Canada Ltd, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd, PCC Energy Inc and Talisman Energy Inc.
Pan-Alberta is a unit of Novagas Clearinghouse Ltd, which, in turn, is 49.9 percent owned by NGC and 50.1 percent owned by NOVA Corp.
NGC first acquired its indirect stake in the natural gas aggregator in May 1995, when it became a unit of Novagas.
NGC senior vice-president and general counsel Ken Randolph said he did not expect the lawsuit to have material impact on NGC, regardless of its outcome.
